Are they valid?\n- **Alternative approaches**: Is there a simpler, more effective, or fundamentally different way to achieve the same goal?\n- **Scope appropriateness**: Is this plan solving the right problem at the right level? Is it too narrow or too broad?\n- **Cost vs. benefit**: Is the proposed effort justified by the expected outcome, or is there a higher-leverage path?\n\n### Completeness\n- **Missing requirements**: Are all features fully specified?\n- **Incomplete tasks**: Do tasks have enough detail to implement?\n- **Missing dependencies**: Are task dependencies properly identified?\n- **Missing edge cases**: Are error conditions and edge cases addressed?\n- **Missing tests**: Is testing strategy adequate?\n\n### Correctness\n- **Technical feasibility**: Is the proposed approach technically sound?\n- **Architecture issues**: Are there design flaws or anti-patterns?\n- **Security concerns**: Are there potential vulnerabilities?\n- **Performance issues**: Will the approach scale appropriately?\n- **Integration issues**: Will the changes work with existing code?\n\n### Clarity\n- **Ambiguous requirements**: Are any requirements unclear or open to interpretation?\n- **Vague tasks**: Do tasks clearly specify what needs to be done?\n- **Missing context**: Is there sufficient background for implementers?\n- **Conflicting statements**: Are there contradictions in the plan?\n\n### Implementation Quality\n- **Over-engineering**: Is the solution more complex than necessary?\n- **Under-engineering**: Is the solution too simplistic for the problem?\n- **Code organization**: Is the proposed file structure sensible?\n- **Naming consistency**: Are names clear and consistent throughout?\n\n## Output Format\nReturn ONLY a valid JSON array with no additional text.
